extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of classical literature; scholars and general readers studying Horace's Satires and classical gastronomy
extracted.subtask_description: Annotated/translated excerpt from Horace's Satires II (including the Catius 'rules' on cookery) with critical commentary and notes explaining references, textual variants, and gastronomic precepts. Useful for readers studying classical satire, ancient dining practice, and textual criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve oblong eggs
rubrics_metrics.description: Give good heed to serve eggs of an oblong shape, for they have a better flavour and are whiter than the round; they are firm and enclose a male yoke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer oblong-shaped eggs because of superior flavour, whiteness, firmness and the presence of a 'male yoke' — a specific selection rule for ingredient quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer cabbage from dry lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Cabbage grown on dry lands is sweeter than from farms near the city; nothing is more tasteless than a watered garden's produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select vegetables from well-drained/dry soils rather than irrigated city gardens to ensure better taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenderize tough fowl with diluted Falernian
rubrics_metrics.description: If a friend suddenly drops in upon you of an evening, and you fear that a tough fowl may answer ill to his taste, you will be wise to plunge it alive into diluted Falernian: this will make it tender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pragmatic (though brutal) technique: use diluted Falernian (wine) to tenderize an otherwise tough bird if needed for an unexpected guest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose meadow mushrooms
rubrics_metrics.description: Mushrooms from the meadows are best; others are not to be trusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer field/meadow mushrooms over others; provenance/habitat is a simple but decisive quality marker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish luncheon with fresh black mulberries
rubrics_metrics.description: A man will pass his summers in health, who will finish his luncheon with black mulberries which he has picked from the tree before the sun is trying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fresh, early-picked fruit (black mulberries picked before the sun's heat) as a healthy concluding taste to a meal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mixing strong Falernian with honey when veins are empty
rubrics_metrics.description: Aufidius used to mix his honey with strong Falernian— unwisely; for, when the veins are empty one should admit nothing to them that is not mild. With mild mead you will do better to flood the stomach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match potency of drink to physiological state: when 'veins are empty' (e.g., fasting), prefer mild drinks rather than strong wine mixed into rich condiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies/pairings for costive bowels
rubrics_metrics.description: If the bowels be costive, limpet and common shell-fish will dispel the trouble, or low-growing sorrel — but not without white Coan wine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribe particular foods and an accompanying wine (white Coan) as a dietary remedy; pairing matters for medicinal culinary effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select shellfish by season and source
rubrics_metrics.description: New moons swell the slippery shell-fish, but it is not every sea that yields the choicest kind. The Lucrine mussel is better than the Baian cockle. Oysters come from Circeii, sea-urchins from Misenum, pectinibus patulis iactat se molle Tarentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose shellfish according to lunar timing and provenance: specific locales produce superior specimens; provenance is essential to quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master the theory of flavours before claiming dining skill
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not everyone that may lightly claim skill in the dining art, without first mastering the subtle theory of flavours. Nor is it enough to sweep up fish from the expensive stall, not knowing which are better with sauce, and which, if broiled, will tempt the tired guest to raise himself once more upon his elbow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Culinary skill requires theoretical knowledge (pairings, preparation methods); buying expensive ingredients alone does not substitute for knowing how to prepare them appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer acorn-fed Umbria boar to Laurentian boar
rubrics_metrics.description: From Umbria, fed on holm-oak acorns, comes the boar that makes the round dish bend, when the host would shun tasteless meat; for the Laurentian is a poor beast, being fattened on sedge and reeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose game by feeding/region: acorn-fed Umbria boar is superior to Laurentian boar fattened on inferior fodder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer particular ages/conditions for hare, fish, and fowl
rubrics_metrics.description: Vinea submittit capreas non semper edulis. fecundae leporis sapiens sectabitur armos. piscibus atque avibus quae natura et foret aetas, ante meum nulli patuit quaesita palatum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select animals (hare, fish, fowl) at appropriate ages/conditions for optimal flavour—age and natural condition affect palatability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not obsess over a single culinary point
rubrics_metrics.description: Some there are whose talent lies only in finding new sweets; 'tis by no means enough to spend all one's care on a single point — just as if someone were anxious only that his wines be good, but cared not what oil he poured upon his fish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain balance in menu composition and preparation; attention must be paid to all elements (wine, oil, sauces), not only one specialty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle wine to preserve flavour (avoid straining through linen)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you set Massic wine beneath a cloudless sky, all its coarseness will be toned down by the night air, and the scent, unfriendly to the nerves, will pass off; but the same wine, when strained through linen, is spoiled, losing its full flavour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate handling/storage to improve wine (night air) and avoid damaging practices (straining through linen spoils flavour).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify wine with pigeons' eggs
rubrics_metrics.description: Surrentine wine a knowing man mixes with lees of Falernian, and carefully collects the sediment with pigeons' eggs, for the yolk sinks to the bottom, carrying with it all foreign matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use egg yolks to coagulate and draw down sediment in wine; a specific technical clarifying method is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulate jaded drinkers with particular appetizers
rubrics_metrics.description: A jaded drinker you will rouse afresh by fried prawns and African snails; for after wine lettuce rises on the acid stomach. By ham and sausages rather does it crave to be pricked and freshened. Nay, it would prefer any viands brought smoking hot from untidy cookshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose stimulating hors d'oeuvres (fried prawns, snails, ham, sausages) and hot, strongly-flavoured food to revive palates dulled by wine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study the nature of the compound sauce (ius duplex)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is worth while to study well the nature of the compound sauce. The simple consists of sweet olive oil ... the compound adds to these the chopped herbs, saffron, and Venafran oil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand sauce structure: a 'simplex' base (sweet olive oil) and a 'compound' version with added herbs, saffron, and oil of Venafrum; use appropriate sauce type to complement dishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pair fruits/wines and use correct fruit-wine matches
rubrics_metrics.description: Picenis cedunt pomis Tiburtia suco; nam facie praestant, Venucula convenit ollis; rectius Albanam fumo duraveris uvam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select fruit and wine pairings based on regional/qualitative matches (e.g., Tiburtine juice preferred for certain fruits; Alban smoke for grapes), attending to provenance in pairing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasoning and presentation: pepper and salt arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: primus et invenior piper album cum sale nigro incretum puris circumposuisse catillis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful seasoning (white pepper with black salt) and deliberate arrangement in dishes is part of refined table practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid culinary vices: overcrowding, poor cleanliness, and tawdry display
rubrics_metrics.description: immane est vitium ... vagos piscis urgere catino. magna movet stomacho fastidia, seu puer unctis tractavit calicem manibus, dum furta ligurrit, sive gravis veteri craterae limus adhaesit. vilibus in scopis, in mappis, in scobe quantus consistit sumptus? ... quanto curam sumptumque minorem haec habeant, tanto reprehendi iustius illis, quae nisi divitibus nequeunt contingere mensis!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid: stuffing/displaying too many fish in small dishes, allowing greasy hands to touch serviceware, using vessels with old sediment, and ostentatious but cheap decorations while neglecting essential standards — cleanliness, proportion, and sincere care are fundamental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe provenance, preparation, and service holistically
rubrics_metrics.description: Docte Cati... ducere me auditum... nam quamvis memori referas mihi pectore cuncta, non tamen interpres tantundem iuveris. adde voltum habitumque hominis, quem tu vidisse beatus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete judgment of dining/cooking requires not only memorized rules but attention to the look, bearing and overall presentation of the server/host — service and context affect the culinary experience.
